ai.module.name: High_Stakes_Operational_Corridors
ai.module.summary: Agentic substrate module defining tightly bounded operational corridors for agents acting in high-stakes, low-tolerance environments. Encodes hard constraint tensors, escalation ladders, kill-switch topologies, and regime-gated authorization flows.
ai.module.purpose: Provide RTT operator grammar and substrate-tensor role assignments that enforce strict behavioral corridors, hard constraint surfaces, multi-level authorization gates, and automated escalation protocols for agents operating in domains where errors carry significant consequence (financial, medical, infrastructure, legal, or physical).

engine.description: Core execution substrate that enforces corridor constraints at every action emission point. Acts as the final gate before any consequential action reaches an external system.

profile.description: Operational authority profile. Encodes the agent's permitted scope, authorization level, and domain clearance. Determines which corridor segments are accessible.

signature.description: Action signature layer. Every consequential action emitted by the agent carries a signed payload referencing the authorizing corridor, authorization chain, and timestamp.

diagnostic.description: Real-time corridor health diagnostics. Monitors constraint surface violations, escalation trigger rates, and authorization bottlenecks.

map.description: Topological map of permitted operational corridors. Nodes are authorized action clusters; edges are transition conditions; boundaries are hard constraint surfaces.

example.description: Canonical worked examples: high-stakes financial execution, clinical decision support, infrastructure change management, legal document filing.

extension.description: Extension points for domain-specific constraint engines, external authorization providers, and custom escalation handlers.

index.description: Searchable index of all corridor artifacts: constraint definitions, authorization records, escalation logs, incident reports.

reference.description: Normative reference material: RTT constraint algebra, corridor topology axioms, authorization grammar specifications.

template.description: Reusable scaffold templates for corridor configurations, constraint surface definitions, and escalation ladder schemas.

operator.description: Top-level RTT operator grammar layer. Governs how corridor operators compose, gate, and project across the constraint tensor space.

operator_semantics.GATE: Intercept an action emission and evaluate it against the active corridor constraints before permitting or blocking.
operator_semantics.AUTHORIZE: Apply multi-level authorization checks against the agent's authority profile and the action's required clearance.
operator_semantics.ESCALATE: Route a blocked or ambiguous action to a higher-authority entity (human or supervisory agent) for resolution.
operator_semantics.HALT: Immediately suspend all action emissions. Requires explicit RELEASE with authorization before resumption.
operator_semantics.ROLLBACK: Reverse the most recent authorized action sequence up to a declared safe state boundary.
operator_semantics.AUDIT: Emit a full signed audit record of the current action, authorization chain, and corridor state.
operator_semantics.RELEASE: Lift a HALT condition after receiving authorized clearance from the escalation resolution entity.

dimensional.description: Dimensional analysis layer. Ensures that all action tensors are dimensionally compatible with the active corridor's constraint surface before emission.
dimensional.constraint: actions must be dimensionally within the corridor bounds on all axes

dimension_semantics.action_severity: Scalar magnitude of potential consequence; 0.0 = benign, 1.0 = catastrophic.
dimension_semantics.authorization_depth: Number of authorization levels required; 1 = self-authorized, N = N-level approval chain.
dimension_semantics.consequence_radius: Scope of affected systems or entities; local = 0.0, global = 1.0.
dimension_semantics.reversibility_index: Ease of undoing the action; fully reversible = 1.0, irreversible = 0.0.

regime.description: Regime declaration layer. Defines the operational regimes of a high-stakes corridor and the constraint profiles active in each.

regimes.description: Standard operations within full corridor bounds. All self-authorized actions permitted within scope.
Heightened operational context. Mid-severity actions require secondary authorization.
High-consequence operations. All actions require multi-level authorization; automated HALT on any constraint violation.
Emergency corridor closure. No agent-initiated actions permitted. Supervisory entity required to issue RELEASE.
Post-incident or compliance review regime. Agent may observe and emit AUDIT records only; no consequential actions.

drift.description: Corridor boundary drift layer. Monitors whether the agent's action distribution is drifting toward corridor boundary edges, indicating increasing risk of a boundary violation.

coherence.description: Corridor coherence layer. Maintains invariants that ensure the agent's behavior remains logically and ethically consistent within the high-stakes domain.

coherence_anchors.name: Authorization Chain Completeness
coherence_anchors.description: Every consequential action must carry a complete, verifiable authorization chain from the initiating authority to the executing agent.

coherence_anchors.name: Constraint Surface Inviolability
coherence_anchors.description: The agent must never emit an action that exceeds the active regime's max_action_severity or falls below the min_reversibility_index.

coherence_anchors.name: Escalation Completeness
coherence_anchors.description: All ESCALATE operations must produce a documented resolution record before the escalated action may proceed or be abandoned.

coherence_anchors.name: Audit Trail Continuity
coherence_anchors.description: Every action emission, gate evaluation, authorization check, and escalation event must produce an immutable signed audit record.

coherence_anchors.name: Scope Boundary Respect
coherence_anchors.description: The agent must not initiate actions affecting entities or systems outside its declared scope boundary, regardless of authorization level.

coherence_anchors.name: Regime Transition Authorization
coherence_anchors.description: Transitions to more restrictive regimes (e.g., NOMINAL→CRITICAL, any→LOCKDOWN) require an authorized trigger event; automatic elevation is permitted. Transitions to less restrictive regimes always require external authorization.

cross-cutting.description: Cross-cutting concerns layer. Handles observability, compliance reporting, inter-module communication, and policy enforcement that span the entire corridor lifecycle.

dead_man_switch.description: If the corridor enforcer does not receive a heartbeat within the configured interval, it automatically transitions to LOCKDOWN.

escalation_ladder.description: Ordered escalation hierarchy. Each level specifies the target authority, required response SLA, and fallback behavior if the SLA is breached.

action_gate_validator.description: Primary corridor gate. Validates that a proposed action is within the active corridor's constraint surface on all dimensional axes.

authorization_chain_validator.description: Validates completeness and integrity of an action's authorization chain against the active regime's required authorization depth.

regime_transition_validator.description: Validates proposed regime transitions against the corridor's transition authorization rules.

drift_boundary_validator.description: Checks whether the agent's recent action distribution is drifting toward corridor boundary edges and whether any zero-tolerance violations are present.

coherence_anchor_validator.description: Evaluates all required coherence anchors against the current corridor state, flagging any zero-tolerance failures immediately.

audit_record_validator.description: Verifies that an emitted audit record is complete, correctly signed, and references a valid gate_decision_id.

examples.title: High-Value Financial Trade Execution
examples.description: An agent executing a $50M block equity trade. Requires ELEVATED regime, 2-level authorization chain, and full audit trail before order submission.
examples.outcome: Trade executed. Audit record AUDIT-2026-0923-001 filed. No coherence anchor violations.

examples.title: Clinical Dosing Recommendation Under Uncertainty
examples.description: An agent proposing a dosing adjustment for a high-risk patient. Ambiguous case triggers mandatory ESCALATE to on-call physician before any recommendation is finalized.
examples.outcome: Recommendation finalized after physician authorization. Escalation resolved within SLA.

examples.title: Infrastructure Change During Incident
examples.description: An agent attempting a high-severity network reconfiguration during an active outage. Dead man switch fires after heartbeat loss; corridor transitions to LOCKDOWN. Human operator issues RELEASE.
examples.outcome: LOCKDOWN lifted after operator RELEASE. Reconfiguration resubmitted under CRITICAL regime with 3-level auth.

external_authorization_provider.description: Replace the built-in authorization chain evaluator with an external identity and access management system (e.g., OAuth2, RBAC engine, hardware HSM).

domain_constraint_engine.description: Plug in a domain-specific constraint surface calculator (e.g., regulatory rule engine, risk scoring model).

escalation_handler.description: Override default escalation routing with a custom handler (e.g., PagerDuty integration, Slack workflow, ticketing system).

immutable_audit_store.description: Route audit records to an external immutable store (e.g., blockchain ledger, WORM storage, SIEM).
